title: Compute Optimizer, rightsizing and idle resource detection

videos.script: The cheapest saving on any bill is something nobody uses. It costs the same every hour, it does nothing, and removing it changes nothing for anybody. {{idle}} You will make the classic four in the lab. A disk attached to nothing, an idle address, an instance stopped for now, and the snapshot of a volume that is gone. Then a program finds them and prices them. {{four}} Then rightsizing. Two weeks of use, four instances, and a rule that reads the busiest hours of CPU and the most memory ever held. Two get smaller. One cannot, because of memory. And one is too small, which is the finding people forget to read. {{size}} You will see what Compute Optimizer adds, and what it cannot see without an agent. {{optimizer}} And the largest saving of the lesson, which changes no instance at all: turning off what nobody uses at night. {{night}}
